examples.description: `merge_invents_a_match.eml` runs a dedup job one sweep at a time and, for every merge, asks whether any original member of one side matched any original member of the other under the same matcher. It compares against the identical job with normalisation moved to compare time.

examples.title: Path resolved twice — the check and the write agreed on the name, not the document
examples.description: `path_resolved_twice.eml` runs three requests against every point at which a rename can be interleaved, under two handlers: one that resolves the name twice (once to authorise, once to act) and one that resolves it once and carries the identity.

examples.title: Rate numerator outgrows denominator — the clamp removed the evidence and kept the error
examples.description: `rate_numerator_outgrows_denominator.eml` computes a conversion rate three ways — with mismatched populations, with the mismatch clamped to 100%, and with both sides drawn from the same population — and reports how many segments each one gets wrong.

examples.title: Rollup double counts shared parent — the thing it is walking is not a tree
examples.description: `rollup_double_counts_shared_parent.eml` runs the recursive rollup and a set-based rollup that visits each node once, then attributes the gap to specific nodes by counting how many distinct root-to-node paths reach each one.

examples.title: Survivor id still referenced — the rows vanished from one report and stayed in the other
examples.description: `survivor_id_still_referenced.eml` merges two customer records two ways — hard delete, and tombstone with a redirect — then runs two ordinary reports over each result and compares them against the pre-merge totals.

examples.title: Abandoned work still lands — the caller stopped waiting and the work did not stop working
examples.description: `abandoned_work_still_lands.eml` runs six requests through three handlers — deadline only, deadline plus a cancel signal, and deadline plus an idempotency key — and compares what the user was **told** against what the store ends up holding.

examples.title: Aggregates that do not decompose — four survived partitioning, three did not, and the call sites are identical
examples.description: `aggregates_that_do_not_decompose.eml` computes seven aggregates over sixteen values both whole and per-partition, at three partition sizes, and reports which ones agree at every size.

examples.title: Attribution window picks the winner — same model, same data, decided by a number in a config file
examples.description: `attribution_window_picks_the_winner.eml` holds last-touch attribution fixed and sweeps only the lookback window, reporting per-channel credit, the winner, and how many conversions end up attributed to nobody.

examples.title: Batch boundary changes order — every batch was handled correctly and the answer was wrong
examples.description: `batch_boundary_changes_order.eml` runs the same sort-and-dedup pipeline at seven batch sizes over twelve records and compares each result against the batch-free answer.

examples.title: Cancel is not idempotent — both designs cancel correctly once
examples.description: `cancel_is_not_idempotent.eml` applies cancel one, two and three times to the same booking under two designs — cancel-as-delta and cancel-as-target-state — and reads the resulting seats and refunds back out.

examples.title: Cancel lands between check and act — accepted, recorded, and too early to matter
examples.description: `cancel_lands_between_check_and_act.eml` sweeps a cancellation's arrival across every tick of a six-step operation, under three placements of the `if cancelled` check, and counts how many arrival times produce the effect anyway.

examples.title: Cancelled work still holds its slot — the pool ran out on a request that was fine
examples.description: `cancelled_work_still_holds_its_slot.eml` replays a twelve-request stream through a three-slot pool under two release placements, and reports the pool over time plus which request first gets refused.

examples.title: Flush timer is a debounce — the latency guarantee held while the system was idle
examples.description: `flush_timer_is_a_debounce.eml` replays three arrival streams through two buffer implementations and reports the worst latency any record actually experienced, against the bound the timer is supposed to provide.

examples.title: Last batch takes a different path — the remainder is zero in every fixture
examples.description: `last_batch_takes_a_different_path.eml` runs every input length from 0 to 12 through a buffered writer with batch size 4, and checks whether the records that left through the drain path got the same treatment as the rest.

examples.title: Last touch vs first touch — four models, different winners, identical totals
examples.description: `last_touch_vs_first_touch.eml` scores four channels under four attribution models over eight conversions, computes each model's ranking, and reports how far channels move.

examples.title: Partial batch failure retries everything — one record that can never succeed rewrote every record that already had
examples.description: `partial_batch_failure_retries_everything.eml` sends six records — one of them permanently bad — through three writers, and counts what the store holds afterwards plus how many records were delivered more than once.

examples.title: Rollback can fail too — every state it can stop in is one the system cannot name
examples.description: `rollback_can_fail_too.eml` sweeps every cancellation point of a four-step operation against every undo that can refuse, and classifies the resulting state.

examples.title: Shared cause has no unique split — every factor was necessary, none was sufficient, and the form has one box
examples.description: `shared_cause_has_no_unique_split.eml` runs a necessity test on every factor of three incidents — remove it, does the outcome still happen — then applies five allocation rules and reports how often they disagree.

examples.title: Two systems both claim it — both reports were honest and their sum was not
examples.description: `two_systems_both_claim_it.eml` runs two attribution platforms over the same ten conversions, reports each one's internal reconciliation, then compares the naive sum against reality and attributes the excess.

examples.title: Usage reported as effect — the metric was largest where the effect was zero
examples.description: `usage_reported_as_effect.eml` carries a hidden per-user field saying what each user would have done *without* the feature, computes the reported metric and the true lift side by side, and sweeps the rollout to show which of the two moves.

examples.title: Commuting until a third step arrives — the pair was interchangeable, the pipeline stopped it being a pair
examples.description: `commuting_until_a_third_step_arrives.eml` measures whether two steps commute, then measures the same two steps with one more placed between them.

examples.title: Coverage through one caller is not coverage — half the helper has never run
examples.description: `coverage_through_one_caller_is_not_coverage.eml` instruments a four-branch helper with a hit counter and runs it from two callers.

examples.title: The default chosen for the first caller — and the aggregate that hides it
examples.description: `default_chosen_for_the_first_caller.eml` runs one `average()` with one empty-input default past two callers for whom that default means opposite things.

examples.title: Each stage keeps a different invariant — 3 of 3 checks pass, 1 of 4 invariants survives
examples.description: `each_stage_keeps_a_different_invariant.eml` runs three stages that each name and keep one invariant, then evaluates four invariants at every stage boundary.

examples.title: Each stage verified, nobody verified the seam — three green checks and 130 units of missing money
examples.description: `each_stage_verified_nobody_verified_the_seam.eml` runs a three-stage pipeline over six billing rows, evaluates each stage's own check, and then asks what happened to the money.

examples.title: The precondition only one caller guarantees — a share of 6.0
examples.description: `helper_precondition_only_one_caller_guarantees.eml` runs one helper — `max(xs) / sum(xs)` — over two callers' input sets and counts the answers that land outside the range its name implies.

examples.title: Idempotence does not compose — three retry-safe routines, two retry-unsafe pairs
examples.description: `idempotence_does_not_compose.eml` measures `f(f(x)) == f(x)` for three cleanup routines, then measures the same property for every ordered pair built from them.

examples.title: Normalisation makes the old tests unreachable — 8 cases, 3 doing work, coverage down
examples.description: `normalisation_makes_the_old_tests_unreachable.eml` puts a normaliser in front of a router and measures what happened to the existing test suite.

examples.title: The not-found sentinel meets negative indexing — a miss returns the last row
examples.description: `not_found_sentinel_meets_negative_indexing.eml` runs six lookups against a four-row table under a guarded and an unguarded call style.

examples.title: Order decides which defect you find — two real bugs, one ticket
examples.description: `order_decides_which_defect_you_find.eml` runs seven batches through two validation stages in both orders and counts what gets reported.

examples.title: Returns a copy, the second caller assumed in place — the call site is identical
examples.description: `returns_a_copy_second_caller_assumed_in_place.eml` calls one cleaning helper two ways over the same input and reports what each caller ends up holding.

examples.title: The pair reaches a state neither part lists — 3 of 3, 3 of 3, and an illegal pair
examples.description: `the_pair_reaches_a_state_neither_part_lists.eml` drives two state machines from one event stream, exhaustively over every sequence of length three, and collects the combined states that actually occur.

examples.title: The safe range of a composition — neither the union nor the intersection
examples.description: `the_safe_range_of_a_composition.eml` sweeps every integer input from 0 to 100 through two functions with documented safe ranges and reads the composition's safe set off the results.

examples.title: Upstream changed scale, downstream kept thresholds — both test suites green, the report worthless
examples.description: `upstream_changed_scale_downstream_kept_thresholds.eml` scores twelve inputs on the old scale and the new one, buckets both with the *same unchanged* code, and compares the distributions.

examples.title: The upstream guard makes the downstream guard dead — and the dead one is wrong
examples.description: `upstream_guard_makes_the_downstream_guard_dead.eml` runs six orders through two validators in series, then through the second one alone.

examples.title: No observable distinguishes the two — 1800 observations, zero disagreements
examples.description: `no_observable_distinguishes_the_two.eml` runs an aliasing store and a copying store side by side and counts how many observations tell them apart.

examples.title: Both sides share the normaliser — 4 behaviours change, the suite sees 0
examples.description: `both_sides_share_the_normaliser.eml` runs the same behaviours under two test styles and measures exactly how much sharing a helper costs.

examples.title: Over-invalidation hides a broken cache key — and the cache never worked
examples.description: `over_invalidation_hides_a_broken_cache_key.eml` sweeps a cache's flush interval and reports when a key that drops a field starts answering.

examples.title: Repairing in the wrong order loses data — a compensating pair cannot be fixed one side at a time
examples.description: `repairing_in_the_wrong_order_loses_data.eml` runs four deployment sequences against a writer and a reader that agree on the wrong field name.

examples.title: The arbiter asks one of the parties — A wins 4 of 4, and is right once
examples.description: `the_arbiter_asks_one_of_the_parties.eml` resolves disputes between two services three ways and grades each against the event log.

examples.title: The disagreement was resolved by widening the tolerance
examples.description: `the_disagreement_was_resolved_by_widening_the_tolerance.eml` sweeps a reconciliation tolerance and measures what it admits besides the difference it was chosen for.

examples.title: The golden was regenerated by the code — 4 of 4 real changes found, then 0
examples.description: `the_golden_was_regenerated_by_the_code.eml` applies a set of changes to a renderer and asks each one twice: does it differ from the frozen golden, and does it differ from a golden regenerated from the changed code.

examples.title: The independent check is a translation — measured by where it agrees
examples.description: `the_independent_check_is_a_translation.eml` compares three implementations and finds the measurement that separates a second opinion from a transcription.

examples.title: The majority is three copies — 4 members, 2 opinions
examples.description: `the_majority_is_three_copies.eml` puts four implementations to a vote and measures how much evidence the vote actually contains.

examples.title: The monitor reads the cache it monitors — 0 of 6 stale ticks caught
examples.description: `the_monitor_reads_the_cache_it_monitors.eml` grades three freshness monitors against what was actually served.

examples.title: The more precise answer wins — precision is printed, accuracy is not
examples.description: `the_more_precise_answer_wins.eml` puts a four-decimal estimate and a whole-number estimate against a computed truth.

examples.title: The noisiest check is relaxed first — 7 of 7 defects caught, then 4
examples.description: `the_noisiest_check_is_relaxed_first.eml` runs a threshold-tuning policy for several rounds and measures what the suite can still catch after each one.

examples.title: The safety net is load-bearing — and it is the only correct code in the pipeline
examples.description: `the_safety_net_is_load_bearing.eml` measures what fraction of a pipeline's correct output arrives through the reconciliation pass rather than through the path that is supposed to produce it.

examples.title: Two defects cancel in the round trip — and half a fix is worse than none
examples.description: `two_defects_cancel_in_the_round_trip.eml` runs an encoder and a decoder that are both wrong, through the only test either of them has.

examples.title: Two off-by-ones preserve the count — so the length check goes quiet
examples.description: `two_off_by_ones_preserve_the_count.eml` slides a window whose start is one late and whose end is one late, and reports what a length check can see.

examples.title: Validated on records that already passed — a clean run over real production data
examples.description: `validated_on_records_that_already_passed.eml` runs a validator over the store it produced, and over the submissions that store came from.

examples.title: One fact counted as three sources — 4 systems agree, 2 origins exist
examples.description: `one_fact_counted_as_three_sources.eml` traces each system's answer back to where it came from and counts distinct origins rather than distinct systems.

examples.title: The exception outlived its reason — 5 of 6 rows removed for a condition that is false
examples.description: `the_exception_outlived_its_reason.eml` evaluates the stated reason for an exclusion against the rows the exclusion currently removes.

examples.title: The record says what was decided — 6 of 6 answered, 0 of 6 checkable
examples.description: `the_record_says_what_was_decided.eml` tries to re-derive every decision from each of two records and counts how many it can reach.

examples.title: The rerun seeds from the last run — and the measurement refused the premise
examples.description: `the_rerun_seeds_from_the_last_run.eml` runs a warm-started and a cold-started chain over the same daily data, with the same pass cap so the seed is the only difference.

examples.title: The resolution is cited in the next dispute — 5 decisions, 1 observation
examples.description: `the_resolution_is_cited_in_the_next_dispute.eml` runs the same disputes under two policies and counts how often each one actually looked at evidence.

examples.title: Both parties assumed the other checked it — 3 unchecked, all 3 seams
examples.description: `both_parties_assumed_the_other_checked_it.eml` offers every item to both parties' ownership rules and computes the four regions.

examples.title: Closed because it stopped being reported — 485 occurrences after closure, 0 reports
examples.description: `closed_because_it_stopped_being_reported.eml` evaluates a "no reports for three periods" closure rule against what the defect was actually doing.

examples.title: Filed against where it surfaced — 1 site named, 4 affected
examples.description: `filed_against_where_it_surfaced.eml` applies two fixes to the same pipeline — one at the reported location, one at the source — and measures every consumer.

examples.title: Finding outruns fixing — same capacity, same count fixed, 127 against 71
examples.description: `finding_outruns_fixing.eml` simulates a defect queue under two work orders with identical throughput.

examples.title: One report, two mechanisms — 3 items named, 7 wrong, 2 causes
examples.description: `one_report_two_mechanisms.eml` takes an honest, well-evidenced defect report and measures what its *shape* does to the fix.

examples.title: Severity assigned before scope was measured — 0 inversions, then 1
examples.description: `severity_assigned_before_scope_was_measured.eml` runs the same three findings over two populations and counts how often triage-by-witness ranks them wrongly.

examples.title: The checker inherits the builder's vocabulary — 6 of 6 named, 0 of 6 unnamed
examples.description: `the_checker_inherits_the_builders_vocabulary.eml` measures a doc-led search's recall, split by whether the defect's class has a name in the docs.

examples.title: The fix moved the boundary — 0 disagreements on every integer tested
examples.description: `the_fix_moved_the_boundary.eml` runs two repairs for the same boundary defect over two domains and measures where they come apart.

examples.title: The guard stopped being able to fail — same green, 1 guard alive, then 0
examples.description: `the_guard_stopped_being_able_to_fail.eml` drills every test in a suite by breaking the code it guards and re-running it.

examples.title: The handoff loses what has no field — 4 of 6 decidable, and one new field bought 0
examples.description: `the_handoff_loses_what_has_no_field.eml` runs each of the receiver's decisions twice: from the transmitted subset, and from everything the sender knew.

examples.title: The regression test locks in the workaround — green in the 2 states where the system is wrong
examples.description: `the_regression_test_locks_in_the_workaround.eml` classifies every assertion in a suite against the rule it was supposed to protect.

examples.title: The repro succeeds for another reason — 140 with the defect on, 140 with it off
examples.description: `the_repro_succeeds_for_another_reason.eml` measures whether a reproduction script is sensitive to the defect it was filed against.

examples.title: The second party finds a different class — 5 found against 7, and 1 that mattered
examples.description: `the_second_party_finds_a_different_class.eml` runs two searchers over one defect population and computes every region of the overlap.

examples.title: The verifier reran the fixer's script — 0 escapes, and 9 inputs never seen
examples.description: `the_verifier_reran_the_fixers_script.eml` runs three input sets against the same repair and counts what each can find.

examples.title: Two findings, one defect — 2 causes each, 1 in the intersection
examples.description: `two_findings_one_defect.eml` measures what routing two reports to two owners destroys.

examples.title: Bucketed by when it arrived — the totals reconcile and the shape does not
examples.description: `bucketed_by_when_it_arrived.eml` builds a daily series two ways from the same 18 events.

examples.title: Each step is of those who reached it — five 90% steps make 59%, and fixing any one gains the same
examples.description: `each_step_is_of_those_who_reached_it.eml` computes the end-to-end rate and the per-step losses from the same five rates, then tries improving each step in turn.

examples.title: Passed means did not raise — perfect on 2 of 4, blind on the other 2
examples.description: `passed_means_did_not_raise.eml` runs four broken variants of the same function through a smoke test and a value test.

examples.title: The absence was created by the filter — same loss, one keeps the answer
examples.description: `the_absence_was_created_by_the_filter.eml` runs two pipelines with comparable drop rates over the same 40 records and compares each reported rate against the true one.

examples.title: The caveat does not survive the second hop — 3 of 3 qualifiers gone, number unchanged
examples.description: `the_caveat_does_not_survive_the_second_hop.eml` walks one payload through four consumers and asks what is left at each.

examples.title: The clarification arrives after the decision — 3 wrong reviews, and waiting 3 days fixes all of them
examples.description: `the_clarification_arrives_after_the_decision.eml` replays every decision at its own time and again with everything that eventually arrived.

examples.title: The counterexample outside the generator — 2000 inputs found 0, 160 found 52
examples.description: `the_counterexample_outside_the_generator.eml` checks two real implementations of integer division against each other and varies the sample count and the sample range separately.

examples.title: The id answers which record, not which person — 10 accounts, 6 people
examples.description: `the_id_answers_which_record_not_which_person.eml` counts new signups two ways from the same rows.

examples.title: The qualifier changes the number — a 40-point drop and zero change in the service
examples.description: `the_qualifier_changes_the_number.eml` computes the same uptime figure from one log under a loose rule and a stated one.

examples.title: The search that stopped early — 7 of 11 records never examined, report unchanged
examples.description: `the_search_that_stopped_early.eml` runs the same scanner over a stream it was written for and a stream that outgrew it.

examples.title: The shared rule ranked worst — 0 of 3 against the strict rule, where three different rules got 2 of 3
examples.description: `the_shared_rule_ranked_worst.eml` ranks three teams three ways from one ticket log and compares each ranking with a strict rule applied to everybody.

examples.title: The test asserts the format, not the value — 5 false alarms and 2 blind pairs
examples.description: `the_test_asserts_the_format_not_the_value.eml` measures the two failure directions of a rendered-output assertion separately, on the same function at the same time.

examples.title: Two definitions, one column name — the roll-up says 11 and only 10 people exist
examples.description: `two_definitions_one_column_name.eml` derives both teams' numbers and the true pooled numbers from one event log.

examples.title: Two sweeps, one sentence — 132 of 144 worlds hide behind the same zero
examples.description: `two_sweeps_one_sentence.eml` runs every one-defect world through both sweeps and counts which worlds each one can separate from the clean world.

examples.title: Zero rows, three explanations — 1 of 3 worlds separable, and two probes fix it
examples.description: `zero_rows_three_explanations.eml` runs three worlds through the same query and counts how many of them each set of observations can still tell apart.

examples.title: Everyone was treated, so there is no before - the mix shift hid 2.3 points of a 4.0 effect
examples.description: `everyone_was_treated_so_there_is_no_before.eml` rebuilds month 3 from month 2's mix and month 2 from month 3's, so each cause can be measured separately.

examples.title: Fixing the flagged ones moved the threshold - 3 flagged every round, forever
examples.description: `fixing_the_flagged_ones_moved_the_threshold.eml` runs a relative and an absolute review rule over the same starting population for the same number of rounds.

examples.title: Not deciding had a cost and no owner - waiting overtakes being wrong at week 17
examples.description: `not_deciding_had_a_cost_and_no_owner.eml` computes both costs on the same scale, week by week, so the comparison nobody makes is available to make.

examples.title: Ranked by clicks, then shown first - locks in at 66% and never reaches 100%
examples.description: `ranked_by_clicks_then_shown_first.eml` runs the ranker for five days over items whose quality is fixed, known to the program, and never read by the ranker.

examples.title: The analysis ran until it agreed - 4 of 10 segments up, in data with an effect of exactly zero
examples.description: `the_analysis_ran_until_it_agreed.eml` cuts a flat overall result by segment and counts how many segments have to be tried before one is up.

examples.title: The decision was made before the number arrived - 1 distinct decision across 8 possible results, 4 distinct announcements
examples.description: `the_decision_was_made_before_the_number_arrived.eml` runs the decision over every possible result and counts the distinct decisions, because that - not whether it was read - is the test of whether an analysis mattered.

examples.title: The forecast triggered its own refutation - 100% of the filed error was created by acting on it
examples.description: `the_forecast_triggered_its_own_refutation.eml` computes the observed world, the world the forecast was about, and next year's correction.

examples.title: The holdout denied a real benefit - 320 in the good world, 2200 saved in the bad one
examples.description: `the_holdout_denied_a_real_benefit.eml` runs both worlds to completion and prints them side by side. No probability is assumed anywhere.

examples.title: The holdout is the only thing that can say no - 12.0 without it, 0.0 with it
examples.description: `the_holdout_is_the_only_thing_that_can_say_no.eml` runs two worlds through the same arithmetic: one where the change does nothing, and one where it works.

examples.title: The holdout shrank until it could not decide - and at an effect of 6 it still could
examples.description: `the_holdout_shrank_until_it_could_not_decide.eml` enumerates every possible contiguous holdout of each size - nothing is sampled - and prints the range of measured effects.

examples.title: The holdout was not held out - 50% of the effect recovered, and still the right shape
examples.description: `the_holdout_was_not_held_out.eml` counts which control requests share a cache key with treated traffic, then measures the effect with and without that leak.

examples.title: The second metric was consulted because the first said no - 7 of 8 launches have something to report, with no effect anywhere
examples.description: `the_second_metric_was_consulted_because_the_first_said_no.eml` runs eight hypothetical launches in which the true effect is zero on every metric, and counts how often each rule finds something.

examples.title: The target stopped being a measure - 100% concordance before, no decidable pairs after
examples.description: `the_target_stopped_being_a_measure.eml` computes the proxy and the goal from the same ticket log in both periods, and measures how well the proxy can still rank tickets by the goal.

examples.title: The threshold was set after seeing the result - excludes 3 of 10 where a fixed bar excluded 6
examples.description: `the_threshold_was_set_after_seeing_the_result.eml` enumerates every bar anyone in the room could have defended and asks what the rule can still exclude once the choice is made afterwards.

examples.title: The work moved to where nobody measures - chart says 66% better, system is 9 worse
examples.description: `the_work_moved_to_where_nobody_measures.eml` runs the same job list under both routings, so the comparison is between two policies rather than two measurements.

examples.title: Filed under the first category that matched - every count ranges from 1 to 6 on rule order alone
examples.description: `filed_under_the_first_category_that_matched.eml` runs the same items under all six orderings of the same three rules.

examples.title: Nobody opened a single one - 2 records show what the summary has no column for
examples.description: `nobody_opened_a_single_one.eml` computes the summary and a small sample from the same rows, and checks whether the extra field is redundant with the categories rather than assuming it.

examples.title: Other became the largest category - and every item in it was filed correctly
examples.description: `other_became_the_largest_category.eml` classifies both eras by the same scheme, so the growth of the catch-all is a fact about the arriving population rather than about drift.

examples.title: Renaming the category changed the trend - a 50% drop that is entirely definitional
examples.description: `renaming_the_category_changed_the_trend.eml` counts every month under both rules, so the definitional part of the step separates from the real part.

examples.title: The action items were closed, not done - 6 of 6 closed, 1 of them blocks anything
examples.description: `the_action_items_were_closed_not_done.eml` replays the incident step by step against the post-fix system, because "was the work done" and "would this happen again" are answered by different evidence.

examples.title: The average describes no one - 0 customers within any tolerance of both means
examples.description: `the_average_describes_no_one.eml` counts how many records sit near the mean on both dimensions at four tolerances, and computes the median on the same data.

examples.title: The count is of tickets, not of incidents - reports fell 54% and events did not move
examples.description: `the_count_is_of_tickets_not_of_incidents.eml` builds both quarters from the same underlying events so the two counts can be separated.

examples.title: The fix from last time was in place - 1 of 5 paths closed, and 4 incidents still to come
examples.description: `the_fix_from_last_time_was_in_place.eml` runs every path to the outage against every guard, so "would the existing fix have stopped this" is answered by enumeration rather than by memory.

examples.title: The lesson was filed where nobody looks - 3 of 7 places reach the person who needs it
examples.description: `the_lesson_was_filed_where_nobody_looks.eml` scores each place a lesson can live by the same three properties and computes the reach rather than arguing it.

examples.title: The outlier was removed for being one - 0 instances of the investigated thing survive cleaning
examples.description: `the_outlier_was_removed_for_being_one.eml` computes the statistics with and without the cleaning rule and counts how many genuine slow paths each dataset still contains.

examples.title: The rule outlived its reason - 6 rejections and 0 downstream failures, in both eras
examples.description: `the_rule_outlived_its_reason.eml` runs the same rule against both eras so that "what did it catch" is answered per era rather than in aggregate.

examples.title: The second time was faster, and that is all - MTTR down 56%, hours down unchanged to the hour
examples.description: `the_second_time_was_faster_and_that_is_all.eml` computes both quantities from the same incident list so the two kinds of progress can be told apart.

examples.title: The top three are the same item - one cause spread across three strings outranks every entry
examples.description: `the_top_three_are_the_same_item.eml` groups by the string the log carries and again by the cause the strings stand for.

examples.title: The total is right and every line is wrong - net error zero, six lines off
examples.description: `the_total_is_right_and_every_line_is_wrong.eml` compares each line against its true value and sums the errors, alongside the reconciliation that is actually run.

examples.title: Two taxonomies that do not partition - both totals are 12 and their numbers cannot be added
examples.description: `two_taxonomies_that_do_not_partition.eml` labels every defect under both schemes, so what each can and cannot say about one population is measured rather than argued.

examples.title: Dividing in place changes the type
examples.description: `dividing_in_place_changes_the_type.eml` - Four compound assignments look alike. One of them changes what the variable is.

examples.title: Nobody calls the documented endpoint
examples.description: `nobody_calls_the_documented_endpoint.eml` - The documented endpoint carries 3% of the traffic. The one nobody wrote down carries most of it.

examples.title: One counterexample retired a rule
examples.description: `one_counterexample_retired_a_rule.eml` - A rule was removed after its visible failures. How often each policy is right is computed below; no figure is stated here, because a number in a comment is checked by nothing.

examples.title: One customer set the roadmap
examples.description: `one_customer_set_the_roadmap.eml` - One account is 4% of revenue and most of the roadmap.

examples.title: The defect was load bearing
examples.description: `the_defect_was_load_bearing.eml` - The bug was fixed and more callers broke than were ever helped.

examples.title: The demo case became the only tested path
examples.description: `the_demo_case_became_the_only_tested_path.eml` - The example in the README is one shape of input. It is the shape 14 of 18 tests exercise.

examples.title: The deprecation reached the readers
examples.description: `the_deprecation_reached_the_readers.eml` - The deprecation was announced in every channel the team has. How many callers that reached is computed below; stating it here would be a number nothing checks.

examples.title: The error metric has no sign
examples.description: `the_error_metric_has_no_sign.eml` - Two forecasting models are scored by absolute error. The score ranks them equal. They are not the same model.

examples.title: The error text is parsed downstream
examples.description: `the_error_text_is_parsed_downstream.eml` - The error message was reworded to be clearer. Four consumers were matching on the old wording.

examples.title: The guard clause skipped the accounting
examples.description: `the_guard_clause_skipped_the_accounting.eml` - A guard clause was added at the top of a loop. It skipped more than the record it was aimed at.

examples.title: The incident everyone remembers
examples.description: `the_incident_everyone_remembers.eml` - The outage nobody will forget cost less than the class nobody can name.

examples.title: The last point is the whole trend
examples.description: `the_last_point_is_the_whole_trend.eml` - The last month is down. The year is up. Both are read off the same twelve numbers.

examples.title: The range and the slice disagree about the end
examples.description: `the_range_and_the_slice_disagree_about_the_end.eml` - Two constructs in one language, both written [a:b], and they do not mean the same b.

examples.title: The reading and the number are not the same record
examples.description: `the_reading_and_the_number_are_not_the_same_record.eml` - The log stores readings as text. The report parses them with `float()`. One of those two holds a fact the other cannot.

examples.title: The unspecified order became the contract
examples.description: `the_unspecified_order_became_the_contract.eml` - The documentation says the order is unspecified. Seven of nine callers depend on it.

examples.title: Each team minimised its own cost
examples.description: `each_team_minimised_its_own_cost.eml` - Four teams, four correct decisions, one total. Whether the total is the smallest available is computed below.

examples.title: Muting the alert removed the only evidence
examples.description: `muting_the_alert_removed_the_only_evidence.eml` - Two alerts were muted in the same week. Their histories since are identical. Only one of the two conditions stopped.

examples.title: Nobody can prove any of them is removable
examples.description: `nobody_can_prove_any_of_them_is_removable.eml` - Eleven workarounds, each added for a condition that was real. How many can be shown to be dead is computed below, and it is not the same as how many are dead.

examples.title: One flag per incident and no tested combination
examples.description: `one_flag_per_incident_and_no_tested_combination.eml` - Twelve flags, one per incident, each added by someone who was right. How many live combinations were ever tested is computed below.

examples.title: The available response was to add a person
examples.description: `the_available_response_was_to_add_a_person.eml` - The system cannot be changed this quarter, so a person checks the output. What that catches is computed below.

examples.title: The exception was caught where it could be caught
examples.description: `the_exception_was_caught_where_it_could_be_caught.eml` - The handler sits at the top of the request, because that is the function this team owns. How many of the failures it catches it can answer correctly is computed below.

examples.title: The fix was applied to the input instead
examples.description: `the_fix_was_applied_to_the_input_instead.eml` - The consumer belongs to another team, so the input is cleaned before it gets there. What that covers is computed below.

examples.title: The log covers the paths we suspected
examples.description: `the_log_covers_the_paths_we_suspected.eml` - Logging was added to the paths that had failed before. The logs now say those paths are where the failures are.

examples.title: The oldest one is the one nobody questions
examples.description: `the_oldest_one_is_the_one_nobody_questions.eml` - The older a workaround is, the more likely its condition is gone and the less likely anyone looks at it. Both halves are computed below.

examples.title: The rate is visible and the request is not
examples.description: `the_rate_is_visible_and_the_request_is_not.eml` - The error rate is on the dashboard, correct to a tenth of a percent, and updated every minute. How many customer complaints it can resolve is computed below.

examples.title: The restart works so the fix never pays
examples.description: `the_restart_works_so_the_fix_never_pays.eml` - The process leaks and gets restarted. Whether fixing it pays is computed below rather than assumed either way.

examples.title: The runbook grew one step per incident
examples.description: `the_runbook_grew_one_step_per_incident.eml` - Fourteen steps, one per incident. How many of them the next incident needs is computed below.

examples.title: The team that can see it cannot change it
examples.description: `the_team_that_can_see_it_cannot_change_it.eml` - The platform team can see every one of these findings. How many of them anyone can act on is computed below.

examples.title: The timeout was raised because it was the adjustable number
examples.description: `the_timeout_was_raised_because_it_was_the_adjustable_number.eml` - The dependency got slower. The timeout was raised. How many calls that changed is computed below.

examples.title: The warning fires where the caller cannot hear it
examples.description: `the_warning_fires_where_the_caller_cannot_hear_it.eml` - The deprecation warning was moved into the call itself, which is the right place for it. How many callers can act on it is computed below.

examples.title: Both sides buffered against the other
examples.description: `both_sides_buffered_against_the_other.eml` - Each side added a queue against the other's variability. What the pair does to the time a unit of work spends in the system is simulated rather than assumed.

examples.title: Each number moves the other so the slope is neither
examples.description: `each_number_moves_the_other_so_the_slope_is_neither.eml` - Test count and build time move together across twelve weeks. What the slope between them measures is computed below.

examples.title: Each side added a shim for the other
examples.description: `each_side_added_a_shim_for_the_other.eml` - Each team wrote a compatibility layer for the other team's changes. How many of them handle the same incompatibility is computed below.

examples.title: Every rollback made the next deploy bigger
examples.description: `every_rollback_made_the_next_deploy_bigger.eml` - A bad deploy is followed by more review before the next one. What that does to the next deploy is simulated rather than argued.

examples.title: Neither date was set by the work
examples.description: `neither_date_was_set_by_the_work.eml` - Each team set its date from the other team's date. Where either date came from is computed below.

examples.title: One interval cannot see which way it feeds back
examples.description: `one_interval_cannot_see_which_way_it_feeds_back.eml` - Two systems take the same shock and respond identically in the first interval. Which of them is amplifying is not in that interval, and is computed here.

examples.title: Shedding load shed what would have relieved it
examples.description: `shedding_load_shed_what_would_have_relieved_it.eml` - Under overload the requests nobody is waiting on are refused first. What that does to the next interval is simulated rather than assumed.

examples.title: The cache decided what was popular
examples.description: `the_cache_decided_what_was_popular.eml` - The cache holds the most requested items, and being held is part of why they are requested. Which items it settles on is simulated rather than assumed.

examples.title: The experiment ran inside the loop
examples.description: `the_experiment_ran_inside_the_loop.eml` - The A/B test was clean: random assignment, one change, a large sample, a clear result. How much of the measured lift is the treatment is computed below.

examples.title: The improvement was the loop settling
examples.description: `the_improvement_was_the_loop_settling.eml` - A metric improved for six months after an initiative started. What else predicts that curve is computed below.

examples.title: The padding was consumed so it was increased
examples.description: `the_padding_was_consumed_so_it_was_increased.eml` - Estimates kept being exceeded, so they were padded. What happened to the padding, and to the accuracy figure everyone watches, is simulated rather than assumed.

examples.title: The return term arrives after the review
examples.description: `the_return_term_arrives_after_the_review.eml` - Each change was reviewed two weeks after it shipped. What each one is worth at two weeks and at six months is computed below.

examples.title: The reviewer got stricter and the author leaned on it
examples.description: `the_reviewer_got_stricter_and_the_author_leaned_on_it.eml` - Review got stricter because defects were escaping, and self-checking got lighter because review was catching things. Where the pair settles is simulated.

examples.title: The static split was the one that diverged
examples.description: `the_static_split_was_the_one_that_diverged.eml` - The scaler moves workers towards whichever queue is deeper, and it acts on numbers that are already stale. Whether that makes it unstable is simulated rather than argued.

examples.title: The target was set by what was asked for
examples.description: `the_target_was_set_by_what_was_asked_for.eml` - The availability target was set to what consumers asked for, and consumers asked for what was published. What any of them needs is computed below.

examples.title: The clause added after the incident
examples.description: `the_clause_added_after_the_incident.eml` - A clause was added to the validator after an incident. What else it rejects is computed below.

examples.title: The compensated sum and the loop disagree
examples.description: `the_compensated_sum_and_the_loop_disagree.eml` - The same numbers added two ways give two answers. Which addition each way performs is computed below.

examples.title: The default swallowed a real zero
examples.description: `the_default_swallowed_a_real_zero.eml` - A missing setting falls back to the default. How many settings that are present also fall back is computed below.

examples.title: The guard was moved for readability
examples.description: `the_guard_was_moved_for_readability.eml` - The two clauses of a condition were swapped so the important one reads first. Which inputs that changes is computed below.

examples.title: The id survived the hop and the type did not
examples.description: `the_id_survived_the_hop_and_the_type_did_not.eml` - Identifiers go out as numbers and come back as numbers. How many of them come back as the same number is computed below.

examples.title: The loop stopped because the steps got small
examples.description: `the_loop_stopped_because_the_steps_got_small.eml` - The solver stops when a step is smaller than the tolerance. How far it still is from the answer at that moment is computed below.

examples.title: The negation was distributed by hand
examples.description: `the_negation_was_distributed_by_hand.eml` - A condition was inverted to turn a skip into a keep. Which inputs the inverted form treats differently is enumerated below.

examples.title: The order the workers finished changed the total
examples.description: `the_order_the_workers_finished_changed_the_total.eml` - Three workers return partial sums and the reducer adds them as they arrive. What the total depends on is computed below.

examples.title: The precision was set by the narrowest hop
examples.description: `the_precision_was_set_by_the_narrowest_hop.eml` - Five systems carry a timestamp and each documents its own resolution. Which one the chain has is computed below.

examples.title: The rounding was applied at every step
examples.description: `the_rounding_was_applied_at_every_step.eml` - Each line is rounded to the cent as it is computed, because a cent is what money is. What that costs over a run is computed below.

examples.title: The schema allowed it and every consumer assumed otherwise
examples.description: `the_schema_allowed_it_and_every_consumer_assumed_otherwise.eml` - The field is an array. How many consumers read anything but the first element is computed below.

examples.title: The test was shorter than the wrap
examples.description: `the_test_was_shorter_than_the_wrap.eml` - The ordering check compares sequence numbers with a greater-than. How many messages that is correct for is computed below.

examples.title: The unit was in the name not in the value
examples.description: `the_unit_was_in_the_name_not_in_the_value.eml` - Every field carries its unit in its name. How many of the arithmetic sites check that name is computed below.

examples.title: The zone was dropped and the value stayed valid
examples.description: `the_zone_was_dropped_and_the_value_stayed_valid.eml` - The zone was dropped at one hop and every timestamp is still a well-formed timestamp. How many of them now mean a different moment is computed below.

examples.title: Which clause actually decided
examples.description: `which_clause_actually_decided.eml` - Access is granted if the caller is an administrator or owns the record. How often each of those was the reason is computed below.

examples.title: Nobody has ever passed the second argument
examples.description: `nobody_has_ever_passed_the_second_argument.eml` - The function takes an optional second argument. How many call sites pass it is computed below, and so is what it costs to keep.

examples.title: The column nobody queried
examples.description: `the_column_nobody_queried.eml` - The column has been in the table for three years and no report has ever selected it. What is in it is computed below.

examples.title: The constant was chosen by someone who left
examples.description: `the_constant_was_chosen_by_someone_who_left.eml` - The constant is 4096 and nobody currently on the team knows why. What depends on it is computed below.

examples.title: The fallback runs only when everything is worst
examples.description: `the_fallback_runs_only_when_everything_is_worst.eml` - The fallback path has run four times in three years. What conditions it ran under is computed below, and it is not a coincidence.

examples.title: The fix shipped to the users who stayed
examples.description: `the_fix_shipped_to_the_users_who_stayed.eml` - The fix went out eleven months after the bug. How many of the affected users were still there to receive it is computed below.

examples.title: The interface was shaped by a caller that is gone
examples.description: `the_interface_was_shaped_by_a_caller_that_is_gone.eml` - Six features of this interface exist because of one integration. That integration was retired two years ago. What still depends on each is computed below.

examples.title: The limit was never reached so it was never wrong
examples.description: `the_limit_was_never_reached_so_it_was_never_wrong.eml` - The limit has been in the config for four years and has never been hit. What is known about the code behind it is computed below.

examples.title: The name outlived the thing it named
examples.description: `the_name_outlived_the_thing_it_named.eml` - The product was renamed four years ago. Where the old name still is, and what it now means in each place, is computed below.

examples.title: The quiet hours are somebody elses peak
examples.description: `the_quiet_hours_are_somebody_elses_peak.eml` - Deploys go out at two in the morning, when traffic is lowest. Whose traffic is lowest is computed below.

examples.title: The reporters are not the affected
examples.description: `the_reporters_are_not_the_affected.eml` - Forty-one people reported the bug. How many hit it is computed below, and the two numbers are about different populations.

examples.title: The rollback has never been run
examples.description: `the_rollback_has_never_been_run.eml` - Every migration ships with a rollback. How much of the data a rollback would return is computed below.

examples.title: The schema still enforces a rule that ended
examples.description: `the_schema_still_enforces_a_rule_that_ended.eml` - Six constraints in the schema encode business rules. How many of those rules are still policy is computed below.

examples.title: The team inherited the oncall and not the decisions
examples.description: `the_team_inherited_the_oncall_and_not_the_decisions.eml` - The current team has owned this service for eleven months. Which decisions the last year of pages trace back to is computed below.

examples.title: The team is on the fast network
examples.description: `the_team_is_on_the_fast_network.eml` - Every latency measurement the team takes is honest. What population it describes is computed below.

examples.title: The two teams never see the same error
examples.description: `the_two_teams_never_see_the_same_error.eml` - The client team sees failures the server team cannot find. Both dashboards are correct, and what each one can contain is computed below.

examples.title: Enforcement decayed with distance from the author
examples.description: `enforcement_decayed_with_distance_from_the_author.eml` - The convention is followed closely in the files its author touches and loosely elsewhere. The gradient is computed below.

examples.title: Fixing the retry storm let the cache go cold
examples.description: `fixing_the_retry_storm_let_the_cache_go_cold.eml` - The retry storm was fixed and the cache hit rate fell. What the retries had been doing is computed below.

examples.title: Silent corruption became a visible error graph
examples.description: `silent_corruption_became_a_visible_error_graph.eml` - Validation was added and the error rate went from near zero to four percent. What changed is computed below.

examples.title: The breach was priced by who found it
examples.description: `the_breach_was_priced_by_who_found_it.eml` - Eight incidents of the same rule being broken. What each one cost the team that broke it is computed below, alongside what it cost the company.

examples.title: The dedup removed the copy that was the backup
examples.description: `the_dedup_removed_the_copy_that_was_the_backup.eml` - Duplicate storage was removed and 40% of the bill went with it. What each duplicate had been doing is computed below.

examples.title: The environment was booked by whoever booked first
examples.description: `the_environment_was_booked_by_whoever_booked_first.eml` - One staging environment, booked first-come. Who gets it and who needs it are computed below.

examples.title: The escalation bought time that was not spare
examples.description: `the_escalation_bought_time_that_was_not_spare.eml` - Seven requests were escalated this quarter and all seven were served first. Where the time came from is computed below.

examples.title: The fix made the next bottleneck the unknown one
examples.description: `the_fix_made_the_next_bottleneck_the_unknown_one.eml` - The slowest stage was made four times faster. What that did to the pipeline, which stage is the constraint now, and how well that one is understood are all computed below.

examples.title: The index was added for the query that complained
examples.description: `the_index_was_added_for_the_query_that_complained.eml` - Nine indexes, each added after somebody reported a slow query. What they cost and what they save is computed below.

examples.title: The limit was raised for everyone who asked
examples.description: `the_limit_was_raised_for_everyone_who_asked.eml` - The default rate limit has not moved in three years. Which callers are still on it is computed below.

examples.title: The quota went to whoever was in the room
examples.description: `the_quota_went_to_whoever_was_in_the_room.eml` - The quarter's compute budget was divided in a planning meeting. How the shares compare to what each team runs is computed below.

examples.title: The rule binds the party with no leverage
examples.description: `the_rule_binds_the_party_with_no_leverage.eml` - The integration standard applies to every partner. Which partners it has actually been applied to is computed below.

examples.title: The same rule blocks here and warns there
examples.description: `the_same_rule_blocks_here_and_warns_there.eml` - One policy, six pipelines, three enforcement levels. Where the violations end up is computed below.

examples.title: The speedup changed a race that had always won
examples.description: `the_speedup_changed_a_race_that_had_always_won.eml` - Two writers have always raced and one has always won by a wide margin. What the margin was, and what a speedup on the other side does to it, are computed below.

examples.title: The waiver went to whoever knew to ask
examples.description: `the_waiver_went_to_whoever_knew_to_ask.eml` - The policy has an exception process. Which teams used it, and which teams qualified, are two different sets, computed below.

examples.title: Every quarter deferring the upgrade was correct
examples.description: `every_quarter_deferring_the_upgrade_was_correct.eml` - A dependency upgrade was deferred eight quarters running. Each deferral is scored under two different rules below, and the accumulated bill is computed.

examples.title: Full compliance was reached by changing the denominator
examples.description: `full_compliance_was_reached_by_changing_the_denominator.eml` - A security standard reached 100% compliance. How many repositories changed and how many left the denominator are counted separately below.

examples.title: Nobody filed an exception so the rule fits
examples.description: `nobody_filed_an_exception_so_the_rule_fits.eml` - A coding standard has drawn two exception requests in eighteen months, and both were granted. What that low number measures is computed below, against what it is being read as measuring.

examples.title: Silence was recorded as assent
examples.description: `silence_was_recorded_as_assent.eml` - A proposal process counts a non-response as approval. What the approvals mean is computed below by separating the votes that were cast from the votes that were assumed.

examples.title: The complaints stopped but the traffic did not
examples.description: `the_complaints_stopped_but_the_traffic_did_not.eml` - A deprecated API stopped generating complaints and was scheduled for removal on that basis. Complaints and calls are counted separately below.

examples.title: The disk was doubled and the retention policy relaxed
examples.description: `the_disk_was_doubled_and_the_retention_policy_relaxed.eml` - Storage was doubled and was full again in four months. Whether the data rate grew is computed below, separately from whether the policy did.

examples.title: The field was made required by one team
examples.description: `the_field_was_made_required_by_one_team.eml` - A producer added one required field to a shared event. What that cost the producer and what it cost everybody else are computed below.

examples.title: The limit was raised and the polling followed it
examples.description: `the_limit_was_raised_and_the_polling_followed_it.eml` - A rate limit was raised from 60 to 300 requests a minute. What the callers did with the extra allowance is computed below, alongside how often the answer had changed.

examples.title: The log level was set by the writer
examples.description: `the_log_level_was_set_by_the_writer.eml` - Each service team sets its own log level. The bill arrives at a team that cannot change any of them. Both quantities are computed below.

examples.title: The memory limit was doing the design review
examples.description: `the_memory_limit_was_doing_the_design_review.eml` - A query memory limit was raised from 4 GB to 16 GB. What the analysts wrote afterwards is computed below, along with what the old limit had been doing.

examples.title: The objections stopped and so did the objectors
examples.description: `the_objections_stopped_and_so_did_the_objectors.eml` - A design review series records fewer objections every quarter. Where the objections went and where the objectors went are computed separately below.

examples.title: The pool doubled and the backlog did not move
examples.description: `the_pool_doubled_and_the_backlog_did_not_move.eml` - The worker pool was doubled and the overnight backlog is the same length it was. What changed and what did not are computed below.

examples.title: The retry budget was set by the caller
examples.description: `the_retry_budget_was_set_by_the_caller.eml` - Every caller configures its own retry count. What each caller pays and what each caller costs are computed below, and they are not the same number.

examples.title: The test was added to everyones suite
examples.description: `the_test_was_added_to_everyones_suite.eml` - One team added a 40-second test to the shared pre-merge suite. What it protects and what it costs are both computed below, and the answer is not that the test is bad.

examples.title: Three times the runners and the same queue
examples.description: `three_times_the_runners_and_the_same_queue.eml` - CI runners went from 8 to 24 and the median wait is back where it started. What changed in between is computed below, and it is not the amount of code.

examples.title: Every request went through her so no form was built
examples.description: `every_request_went_through_her_so_no_form_was_built.eml` - A routing config is written in a format one person understands. What her turnaround does to the case for a self-serve form is computed below.

examples.title: One reviewer on every change and no second reader
examples.description: `one_reviewer_on_every_change_and_no_second_reader.eml` - One engineer reviews every change to a module. What that does to how many people can read it is computed below.

examples.title: The breaker tripped on the limiters own rejections
examples.description: `the_breaker_tripped_on_the_limiters_own_rejections.eml` - A rate limiter and a circuit breaker both protect the same downstream service. What each one sees, and what the pair sees, are computed separately below.

examples.title: The buffer absorbed the signal backpressure needed
examples.description: `the_buffer_absorbed_the_signal_backpressure_needed.eml` - A queue has both a buffer to absorb bursts and backpressure to slow the producer. When each one engages is computed below.

examples.title: The enum grew and the else branch absorbed it
examples.description: `the_enum_grew_and_the_else_branch_absorbed_it.eml` - A status field gained three new values. The field name, the type and the wire format did not change. What each consumer now does with those values is computed below.

examples.title: The expert keeps the recovery time below the threshold
examples.description: `the_expert_keeps_the_recovery_time_below_the_threshold.eml` - A module is hard to debug and one engineer is very good at debugging it. What that does to the case for simplifying it is computed below.

examples.title: The field stopped being null and killed the branch
examples.description: `the_field_stopped_being_null_and_killed_the_branch.eml` - A nullable field was backfilled and now always has a value. What that did to the code written for the null case is computed below.

examples.title: The health check hid the shortfall from the autoscaler
examples.description: `the_health_check_hid_the_shortfall_from_the_autoscaler.eml` - A health check removes unhealthy instances and an autoscaler adds capacity when the fleet is loaded. What each measures is computed below.

examples.title: The id stayed a string and stopped being unique
examples.description: `the_id_stayed_a_string_and_stopped_being_unique.eml` - An order id was globally unique and became unique per tenant. Same field, same string type, same length. When that matters is computed below.

examples.title: The rate field moved from a fraction to a percentage
examples.description: `the_rate_field_moved_from_a_fraction_to_a_percentage.eml` - A discount_rate field carried 0.15 and now carries 15. Same name, same numeric type. Which consumers noticed is computed below.

examples.title: The remediation fixed it before anyone could be told
examples.description: `the_remediation_fixed_it_before_anyone_could_be_told.eml` - Auto-remediation restarts the failing process and alert deduplication suppresses the repeat. What each does, and what the pair does to escalation, are computed below.

examples.title: The sanitiser made the bad input pass validation
examples.description: `the_sanitiser_made_the_bad_input_pass_validation.eml` - A sanitiser and a validator both guard the same intake. What each rejects, and what the pair rejects, are computed separately below.

examples.title: The shim is maintained so the migration never finishes
examples.description: `the_shim_is_maintained_so_the_migration_never_finishes.eml` - A compatibility shim translates between an old schema and a new one. One person maintains it by hand. What that does to the migration is computed below.

examples.title: The timestamp changed from event time to ingest time
examples.description: `the_timestamp_changed_from_event_time_to_ingest_time.eml` - A field called occurred_at changed from the time the event happened to the time the pipeline received it. Same name, same type, same format. What moved is computed below.

examples.title: The tool is slow and the only user is fast
examples.description: `the_tool_is_slow_and_the_only_user_is_fast.eml` - An internal tool takes many steps to do anything. Its recorded task time is good. Who produced that number is computed below.

examples.title: The adoption was measured where there was no alternative
examples.description: `the_adoption_was_measured_where_there_was_no_alternative.eml` - The new internal tool reports 96 percent adoption in its fourth quarter. What the number is measuring is computed below.

examples.title: The boost was a loan and nobody counted the lenders
examples.description: `the_boost_was_a_loan_and_nobody_counted_the_lenders.eml` - A low-priority task held a lock that a high-priority task needed, and medium-priority work ran ahead of both. Priority inheritance fixed it. What the fix cost over the following twelve weeks is computed below.

examples.title: The candidate who could not win decided the winner
examples.description: `the_candidate_who_could_not_win_decided_the_winner.eml` - Seventeen people rank three proposals. One proposal wins under none of the three counting rules. What happens to the result when it is taken off the ballot is computed below.

examples.title: The constraint was on the wrong pair of columns
examples.description: `the_constraint_was_on_the_wrong_pair_of_columns.eml` - A unique constraint on room and start time, protecting a rule about rooms not being double booked. What it accepts and what it refuses is counted below.

examples.title: The cost appeared only when it stopped being paid
examples.description: `the_cost_appeared_only_when_it_stopped_being_paid.eml` - A weekly maintenance job was cancelled after 140 runs that each reported nothing found. When the bill arrived, and who was blamed for it, are computed below.

examples.title: The counter was emptied by whoever read it first
examples.description: `the_counter_was_emptied_by_whoever_read_it_first.eml` - A counter that reports events since the last read, and a second collector added during a region migration. What each collector sees afterwards is computed below.

examples.title: The depth limit was shared with the caller
examples.description: `the_depth_limit_was_shared_with_the_caller.eml` - A recursive tree walker is documented as supporting trees up to 497 levels deep. The same record that passes in the test suite fails in the request handler. What changed between the two is computed below.

examples.title: The escape was correct at every layer
examples.description: `the_escape_was_correct_at_every_layer.eml` - Customer names are escaped when they arrive and escaped again when they are rendered. What each output route shows is computed below.

examples.title: The hash was uniform and the buckets were not
examples.description: `the_hash_was_uniform_and_the_buckets_were_not.eml` - The hash was tested for uniformity and passed. The bucket occupancy in production is counted below, from the same hash.

examples.title: The latency was measured at the wrong end
examples.description: `the_latency_was_measured_at_the_wrong_end.eml` - Three endpoints were changed to stream their results instead of building the whole response first. The latency dashboard recorded the best week it had ever seen. What the clients saw is computed below.

examples.title: The limit was per key and the caller chose the key
examples.description: `the_limit_was_per_key_and_the_caller_chose_the_key.eml` - The rate limiter allows 100 requests a minute per client, and it has never allowed a bucket to exceed 100. What it allowed in total is computed below.

examples.title: The load test used the shape production never has
examples.description: `the_load_test_used_the_shape_production_never_has.eml` - The load test sends 8000 requests spread evenly over 8 shards. Production sends 8000 requests too. Which numbers the two runs agree on is computed below.

examples.title: The mask removed the value and kept the length
examples.description: `the_mask_removed_the_value_and_kept_the_length.eml` - Customer names and email local parts are masked in the application log, one asterisk per character. How many customers the masked log still identifies uniquely is counted below.

examples.title: The restore was the path that never ran
examples.description: `the_restore_was_the_path_that_never_ran.eml` - The backup has succeeded 412 nights in a row. How much of the restore path that number covers is computed below.

examples.title: Three copies and two places to lose them
examples.description: `three_copies_and_two_places_to_lose_them.eml` - Every shard has three replicas, verified continuously, never fewer. How many shards survive the loss of one rack is computed below.

examples.title: The alert threshold was set from the week it was written
examples.description: `the_alert_threshold_was_set_from_the_week_it_was_written.eml` - An alert fires when requests per second cross 2400. That number was chosen in month 0 as twice the busiest second of the week the alert was written. What it means in each later month is computed below.

examples.title: The audit sampled the records that were easiest to fetch
examples.description: `the_audit_sampled_the_records_that_were_easiest_to_fetch.eml` - An audit sampled 500 of 50000 accounts and found a defect rate of 4 per thousand. What that rate is a rate of is computed below.

examples.title: The buffer was sized for the average and the burst was the point
examples.description: `the_buffer_was_sized_for_the_average_and_the_burst_was_the_point.eml` - Events arrive at 100 a second on average. The buffer holds 200, which is twice the average, and the consumer drains 120 a second. What happens during the burst is computed below.

examples.title: The cheaper path was taken often enough to cost more
examples.description: `the_cheaper_path_was_taken_often_enough_to_cost_more.eml` - A request handler calls five things. The code review flagged the slowest of them. Which one that is depends on a sort order, and both orders are computed below.

examples.title: The compression helped until the data stopped being similar
examples.description: `the_compression_helped_until_the_data_stopped_being_similar.eml` - The archive ingests 1000 GB a month, every month, and has done for a year. What it stores is computed below, along with the capacity forecast that was written in month 1.

examples.title: The deadline was met by moving what counted as done
examples.description: `the_deadline_was_met_by_moving_what_counted_as_done.eml` - 120 features were committed for the quarter. The quarter closed at 79 percent complete. What 79 percent counted is computed below.

examples.title: The error rate fell because the errors moved
examples.description: `the_error_rate_fell_because_the_errors_moved.eml` - Service A's error rate went from 3 percent to 0.2 percent after one change. Where the errors went is computed below.

examples.title: The id was reused after the thing it identified was gone
examples.description: `the_id_was_reused_after_the_thing_it_identified_was_gone.eml` - The audit log holds 20000 references, each one an entity id captured at the time an action was taken. How many of them still name the entity they were written about is computed below.

examples.title: The lock was held across a call that could block
examples.description: `the_lock_was_held_across_a_call_that_could_block.eml` - A cache refresh is guarded by a mutex. The thread pool was raised from 8 to 32 and throughput did not move. What the pool size can and cannot change is computed below.

examples.title: The migration finished and both writers kept writing
examples.description: `the_migration_finished_and_both_writers_kept_writing.eml` - The migration from the old store to the new one completed twelve months ago and was signed off. Both stores are still being written to. What is in each of them is computed below.

examples.title: The ratio was stable and both sides were shrinking
examples.description: `the_ratio_was_stable_and_both_sides_were_shrinking.eml` - Conversion rate held at 3.0 percent for twelve months. What held it there is computed below.

examples.title: The sample size was the thing that changed
examples.description: `the_sample_size_was_the_thing_that_changed.eml` - Three quarters of latency review. Each quarter the team sampled transactions and reported the worst one they saw. The worst got worse every quarter. What else changed is computed below.

examples.title: The throughput doubled and the tail got worse
examples.description: `the_throughput_doubled_and_the_tail_got_worse.eml` - The batch size was raised from 10 to 100. Throughput went from 166 to 416 items a second. What a single request experiences is computed below.

examples.title: The total was capped and the parts were not
examples.description: `the_total_was_capped_and_the_parts_were_not.eml` - The cloud account has a hard spending cap of 10000 a month. Eight services share it. On day 7 the cap fired. Which services stopped is computed below.

examples.title: The work was split evenly and the workers were not
examples.description: `the_work_was_split_evenly_and_the_workers_were_not.eml` - A batch of 2400 documents is split across 8 workers. Every worker gets exactly 300. How long the batch takes, and how long the report says it takes, are computed below.

examples.title: The bug was fixed in the library and the vendored copy stayed
examples.description: `the_bug_was_fixed_in_the_library_and_the_vendored_copy_stayed.eml` - An advisory is published, the library ships a fix, and the dependency scanner reports every service patched. How many are running the fixed code is computed below.

examples.title: The deploy was atomic and the config was not
examples.description: `the_deploy_was_atomic_and_the_config_was_not.eml` - Code is deployed blue-green, so every instance switches at once. Configuration is polled every 60 seconds. What runs during those 60 seconds is computed below.

examples.title: The exchange rate was right and its timestamp was not
examples.description: `the_exchange_rate_was_right_and_its_timestamp_was_not.eml` - A payment is quoted in the customer's currency at authorization and settled three days later at capture. Both conversions use the published rate. The difference is computed below.

examples.title: The fix was verified on the machine that had the fix
examples.description: `the_fix_was_verified_on_the_machine_that_had_the_fix.eml` - A bug reproduces on 4 of 12 hosts. The fix was deployed to one host, verified there, and rolled out. What that verification could and could not have shown is computed below.

examples.title: The flag defaulted differently in two places
examples.description: `the_flag_defaulted_differently_in_two_places.eml` - One feature flag, read by the server and by the browser. Each side has a default for when the flag service cannot be reached. What the two defaults do together is computed below.

examples.title: The limit was on the response and the cost was in the query
examples.description: `the_limit_was_on_the_response_and_the_cost_was_in_the_query.eml` - The API returns at most 20 rows per call and the rate limiter counts calls. What one call costs the database is computed below.

examples.title: The log was sampled and the rare event was the point
examples.description: `the_log_was_sampled_and_the_rare_event_was_the_point.eml` - Request logging was sampled at 1 percent to bring the bill down. What each class of event looks like afterwards is computed below.

examples.title: The metric came from a view that filtered
examples.description: `the_metric_came_from_a_view_that_filtered.eml` - Three metrics are computed from one view. The view excludes cancelled orders. What each metric becomes is computed below.

examples.title: The number was right and the label came from another query
examples.description: `the_number_was_right_and_the_label_came_from_another_query.eml` - A report shows four regions and their totals. The names come from one query and the totals from another, joined by row position. What each region is shown as is computed below.

examples.title: The permission was checked before the data was chosen
examples.description: `the_permission_was_checked_before_the_data_was_chosen.eml` - A search returns the ten highest-scoring documents a user is allowed to see. The user reports that the page is nearly empty. How many results each ordering produces is computed below.

examples.title: The redundancy shared a dependency
examples.description: `the_redundancy_shared_a_dependency.eml` - The service runs in three availability zones. Each zone is measured at 99.9 percent. The availability the three of them actually provide is computed below.

examples.title: The rule was enforced at write time and the data predated it
examples.description: `the_rule_was_enforced_at_write_time_and_the_data_predated_it.eml` - A validation rule was added to the write path eighteen months ago. Every row written since satisfies it. What fraction of the table satisfies it is computed below.

examples.title: The timeout was longer than the caller patience
examples.description: `the_timeout_was_longer_than_the_caller_patience.eml` - The service times out a request after 30 seconds. The client library gives up after 5. What the server is doing between those two numbers is computed below.

examples.title: The two clocks agreed on duration and disagreed on order
examples.description: `the_two_clocks_agreed_on_duration_and_disagreed_on_order.eml` - A request crosses three services and is timestamped at every hop. The end-to-end duration is trusted and the hop ordering is trusted. Only one of them is safe, and which is computed below.

examples.title: The two teams agreed on the word and not the meaning
examples.description: `the_two_teams_agreed_on_the_word_and_not_the_meaning.eml` - Two teams report active users. The growth team says 42000, the platform team says 18000. Both queries are correct and the numbers they produce are computed below.

examples.title: The aggregate was cached and the parts were live
examples.description: `the_aggregate_was_cached_and_the_parts_were_live.eml` - One page shows a total at the top and the rows it totals underneath. The total is cached for five minutes; the rows are queried live. What the two disagree by is computed below.

examples.title: The backup ran nightly and the change was hourly
examples.description: `the_backup_ran_nightly_and_the_change_was_hourly.eml` - The backup has succeeded every night for four hundred nights. The recovery point objective is one hour. What is actually recoverable is computed below.

examples.title: The config was validated at startup and edited at runtime
examples.description: `the_config_was_validated_at_startup_and_edited_at_runtime.eml` - The configuration is validated on load: every field is type-checked, every range is bounded, every reference is resolved. How many of the month's config changes go through that validation is computed below.

examples.title: The count was distinct and the join multiplied the rows
examples.description: `the_count_was_distinct_and_the_join_multiplied_the_rows.eml` - A report joins orders to their line items so it can break revenue down by product category. Three numbers on the same report are computed below.

examples.title: The default sort made the diff unreadable
examples.description: `the_default_sort_made_the_diff_unreadable.eml` - A generated configuration file is regenerated on every build and committed. How much of each diff is a real change is computed below.

examples.title: The encoding was declared and the bytes disagreed
examples.description: `the_encoding_was_declared_and_the_bytes_disagreed.eml` - Every uploaded file declares its encoding, the importer honours the declaration, and the encoding validator passes 100 percent of records. How many names arrive correctly is computed below.

examples.title: The queue had no maximum and the memory did
examples.description: `the_queue_had_no_maximum_and_the_memory_did.eml` - The in-process queue has never rejected a message. How long that can continue is computed below.

examples.title: The record was corrected and the derived copy was not
